title: Inspect tires for wear and damage
summary: Check tread depth, age and damage so you replace a tire before it fails.
tools: Tread depth gauge or a coin

steps.text: Find the wear bar markers: small triangles on the sidewall point to raised bars inside the tread grooves.
If the tread is level with a wear bar anywhere on the tire, replace the tire.
steps.caution: Worn tires lose grip fast on wet roads. Don't wait for the cords to show.

steps.text: Look for cuts, bulges, embedded nails or glass. Turn the wheel slowly to see the whole tire.
Check for cracking on the sidewalls and between the tread blocks; that is a sign of age or underinflation.
Read the four-digit date code on the sidewall (week then year, e.g. 2324 is week 23 of 2024). Replace tires older than five to six years even if they look fine.
Finish by setting the pressure to the values on your spec sheet.
